name: Wang Pan
bio: Wang Pan (王磐, courtesy name Hongze) was a Ming dynasty writer and painter from Gaoyou in Jiangsu. He declined an official career and lived as a private scholar, and he is remembered chiefly for his sanqu, songs written to set tunes in the vernacular-flavoured style of the Yuan lyric.

His best-known songs are satirical. In two of them he mocks the eunuch-officials who travelled the Grand Canal in grand state boats, the trumpet and the sound of its blowing standing for the havoc they brought to the people along the water.

poems.title: 朝天子·詠喇叭 (Chao tian zi · Yong la ba)
poems.author: Wang Pan
poems.text:
喇叭，嗩呐，曲兒小腔兒大。官船來往亂如麻，全仗你抬聲價。
軍聽了軍愁，民聽了民怕。那裡去辨甚麼真共假？
眼見的吹翻了這家，吹傷了那家，只吹的水盡鵝飛罷！
